senses.definition: To push someone roughly; to crowd; to jostle.

quotes.text: There is an hour or two, after the passengers have embarked, which is disquieting and fussy.[…]Passengers wander restlessly about or hurry, with futile energy, from place to place. Pushing men hustle each other at the windows of the purser's office, under pretence of expecting letters or despatching telegrams.
quotes.reference: 1915, G[eorge] A. Birmingham [pseudonym; James Owen Hannay], chapter I, in Gossamer, New York, N.Y.: George H. Doran Company, →OCLC:

examples: I'll have to hustle to get there on time.

quotes.text: Men in dairy lunches were hustling to gulp down the food which cooks had hustled to fry

senses.definition: (transitive) To bundle; to stow something quickly.

quotes.text: There was a person called Nana who ruled the nursery. Sometimes she took no notice of the playthings lying about, and sometimes, for no reason whatever, she went swooping about like a great wind and hustled them away in cupboards.

senses.definition: (transitive) To con, swindle, or deceive, especially financially.
examples: The guy tried to hustle me into buying into a bogus real estate deal.

senses.definition: To play deliberately badly at a game or sport in an attempt to encourage players to challenge one.
(informal) To obtain by illicit or forceful action.
(informal) To sell sex; to work as a pimp.
(informal) To be a prostitute; to exchange use of one's body for sexual purposes for money.

quotes.text: All my life, been hustling / And tonight is my appraisal / 'Cause I'm a hooker selling songs / And my pimp's a record label
quotes.reference: 2018, Brendon Urie, Michael Angelakos, Sam Hollander, Morgan Kibby, Jake Sinclair, Dillon Francis, “Hey Look Ma, I Made It”, in Pray for the Wicked, performed by Panic! at the Disco:

senses.definition: (informal) To serve (a clientele) as a prostitute.

quotes.text: When I was in Morocco I wrote this play ("Playland Blues") about young kids who […] hustle old gay men and closet queens.
quotes.reference: 1976 February 14, Tommi Avicolli, Miguel Pinero, “Miguel Pinero: Prisoner, Playwright, God”, in Gay Community News, volume 3, number 33, page 9:

senses.definition: To dance the hustle, a disco dance.
(informal) To put a lot of effort into one's work.

quotes.text: Frazier and Gary worked for me for free -- for six months -- they didn't take any money from the house. They worked for tips. They both had other jobs, and they came in here and they hustled their ass.

senses.definition: A propensity to work hard and get things done; ability to hustle.

quotes.text: 'It's just natural for the folks here to be indolent,' she said. 'They just haven't got any hustle in them.'

senses.definition: (preceded by a definite article) A type of disco dance, commonly danced to the Van McCoy song The Hustle (1975).
(prison slang) An activity, such as prostitution or reselling stolen items, that a prisoner uses to earn money in prison.

quotes.text: Little Joe never once gave it away / Everybody had to pay and pay / A hustle here and a hustle there / New York City's the place
quotes.reference: 1972, Lou Reed, “Walk on the Wild Side”:

senses.definition: (informal) An activity, especially to achieve a desired goal or make money.
